key.name: history-size
key.description: How many copies to keep. Older ones are dropped first. The history is held in memory only and is never written to disk.

key.name: image-budget-mb
key.description: The most memory, in megabytes, that copied images may use together. The oldest images are dropped first. 0 stops images being kept at all.

key.name: expire-minutes
key.description: Minutes after which a copy is dropped from the history. Pinned snippets never expire. 0 keeps copies until they are pushed out.

key.name: clear-on-lock
key.description: Empty the history when the screen locks. When off, the history is kept in memory across the lock; nothing is recorded while locked either way.

key.name: auto-paste
key.description: After choosing an item in the popup, paste it into the window that had focus. Terminals listed in terminal-apps get Ctrl+Shift+V.

key.name: paused
key.description: While true, copies are not recorded. Toggled from the tile.

key.name: quickclip-open-popup
key.description: Shortcut that opens the clipboard popup. Chosen so it does not take over any GNOME default.

key.name: quickclip-toggle-pause
key.description: Shortcut that pauses or resumes recording. Unset by default.

key.name: ignored-apps
key.description: Desktop app ids whose copies are not recorded. Wayland does not say which app made a copy, so this uses the app focused at the time.

key.name: terminal-apps
key.description: Desktop app ids that paste with Ctrl+Shift+V instead of Ctrl+V.

key.name: pinned
key.description: Text you pinned. The only clipboard content QuickClip stores on disk, and only because you asked it to.
